question: May a kernel-prediction, sample-transformer or hybrid candidate execute without explicit opt-in and provider/artifact-bound per-sample outputs?
hypothesis: Allowing an unbound model result would destroy reproducibility, applicability and permutation semantics, so every external candidate must fail before reconstruction unless its capsule, provider, artifact and sample identities match.

configuration.external_weights: provider and artifact bound when supplied

reproducibility.seed_policy: No stochastic inference is performed; deterministic validation decides admission from content identities and applicability.
reproducibility.determinism: Candidate and external-weight identities include the capsule, algorithm, provider, artifact, applicability and sorted sample identity mapping.

baseline: Use the analytic sample-splat baseline or leave the raw estimate unchanged.
candidate: Execute externally supplied kernel-prediction, point-set/transformer or hybrid sample weights without complete provenance.

result.conclusion: The shortcut is rejected. External model families are executable only as explicitly opted-in Research candidates with provider/artifact/sample-bound outputs; no model file format or trained capability is promoted.

known_failure_domain: The rejection does not disprove kernel-prediction, sample-transformer or hybrid reconstruction.
No trained artifact is shipped or benchmarked by HR.2.
A future provider may define a separately versioned model and inference ABI after evidence exists.
OOD override remains Research-only and reduces reported confidence while retaining the OOD mask.
